page: The Vultr vbm-6c-32gb-amd is a bare metal server featuring an AMD EPYC 4245P processor built on the x86_64 architecture. This dedicated server provides 6 physical cores and 12 vCPUs operating at a base clock speed of 3.8 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.67 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 1920 GB NVMe SSD, and the system includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance type.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance scoring 4538.09 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 49.16 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10% of tested servers. The PassMark memory score of 3263.14 also ranks in the top tier. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a PassMark CPU score of 31542.86 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 26985.31, both falling within the average range. For small-scale language model tasks, the server achieves a top-tier text generation speed of 430.19 tokens/second using a 135M model.

While read-only memory bandwidth is average, reaching 1624.4 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 50.45 GB/sec for large blocks, a notable hardware tradeoff is the weak large-block write memory bandwidth of 23.57 GB/sec, which falls into the bottom 25%. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this bare metal server offers high single-core compute density and substantial local NVMe storage relative to its resource footprint, making it a viable option for workloads requiring dedicated physical resources without the overhead of virtualization.

This server configuration is suited for single-threaded processing tasks, static web serving, database operations, and lightweight machine learning inference using smaller models. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores and local NVMe storage supports consistent execution times for applications sensitive to multi-tenant resource contention.
